Counted exact modular multiplication and shared NTT butterflies

Scope
This contribution supplies literal programs for the nine-instruction WordRAM model
in tcslib, an independent Python interpreter, executable evidence and informal
universal proofs. It does not instantiate the Lean compiler theorem and is not
Lean-checked. Its fixed modulus does not establish an asymptotic multiplication
bound or a new kappa. The sharing optimization is standard; no novelty claim.

1. Exact machine, ABI and charged constants
Fix W=64 and p=65537. Words have arithmetic modulo 2^64. Conditional branches
interpret their operand as a signed two's-complement integer. Only the actual
one/add/sub/mul/load/store/bltz/accept/reject instructions are accepted. The
programs use direct-address arithmetic and branches, so need no implicit address
loads. Interpreter masking and sign conversion implement word semantics; they
are not extra target instructions. There is no target div, shift or remainder.

Scratch S={8,9,10,11,20,...,35}; constants cell 20+i hold p*2^i, zero is cell 10,
one is cell 11, temporary subtraction is cell 9, retained product is cell 8.
Setup is one(11), zero=one-one, one(20), 16 doublings of cell 20, add one,
then 15 doublings into the remaining cells: exactly 35 instructions. The caller
may supply arbitrarily dirty scratch. Cleanup clears every scratch cell except
cell 10, which has remained zero: exactly 19 instructions. No initial zero memory
assumption is needed. A final accept is one charged instruction.

The modular multiply ABI is inputs cells 0,1; output cell 3. The butterfly ABI is
inputs u,b,w at 0,1,2; outputs plus,minus at 3,4. Inputs are in [0,p). Outputs
start arbitrarily dirty. Inputs and every cell outside S union outputs are
unchanged, including negative addresses and arbitrary dirty far memory. All
scratch ends zero. A finite Python dictionary tests sample far addresses; the
universal frame claim follows separately because every write target in the
literal text is an explicitly listed cell and branches make no memory writes.

For composition Builder permits caller-selected nonreserved cells. Butterfly
outputs must be fresh/disjoint from inputs; mul may overwrite one operand since
the initial multiplication reads both before writing. Constants remain live
between setup and cleanup. Fresh twiddles must be supplied as input ABI or built
with Builder.literal: 1 instruction for zero and bit_length(n)+popcount(n)-1
for positive n<2^63. No twiddle construction or caller-side routing is free.
A direct copy is a charged add(dst,src,zero), one instruction. Python generation,
looping and allocation are not charged target work unless translated to emitted
instructions. A fully unrolled fixed-size program has literal immediate cell
addresses; a variable-size runtime implementation requires further work.

2. Universal modular multiplication invariant
For 0<=a,b<p, x=a*b <=65536^2=2^32 <p*2^16. Emit mul(output,a,b). Then for
i=15,14,...,0 perform:
  tmp := x - p*2^i
  if tmp<0 branch past the next instruction
  x := tmp + zero
This is three literal instructions; the third executes precisely when the
subtraction is nonnegative. At stage entry 0<=x<p*2^(i+1). If x<p*2^i the branch
keeps x in [0,p*2^i). Otherwise subtracting p*2^i gives the same interval. The
residue modulo p is invariant. Induction leaves 0<=x<p and x congruent to ab,
hence x=ab mod p. All products, thresholds and signed differences have absolute
value at most 2^32; W=64 therefore makes every signed comparison faithful and
there is no product truncation. This proof covers all p^2 input pairs.

The chosen subtractions are exactly the binary expansion of q=floor(ab/p),
where 0<=q<=65535. Thus the modular-multiply body has 49 static instructions and
33+popcount(q) dynamic instructions: one product, 32 subtract/branch instructions,
and popcount(q) copies. The complete generic-cleanup program has 104 static
instructions and 88+popcount(q)<=104 dynamic instructions, including halt. The
extra clearing of unused retained cell 8 is deliberately counted.

3. Sharing gives a paid machine saving
For u,b,w in [0,p), let v=bw mod p. The fused butterfly computes v once and
returns ((u+v) mod p,(u-v) mod p). The reference unfused program computes the
same v twice, once for each output, with identical setup/cleanup/output ABI.
The latter is a deliberately explicit recomputation baseline, not an assertion
about the existing project's best implementation.

Sum uses x=u+v in [0,2p-2], followed by one threshold-p reduction. Difference
uses x=u+p-v in [1,2p-1], followed by one threshold-p reduction. Each therefore
needs at most one subtraction. The difference is congruent to u-v modulo p.
No signed overflow occurs. The output blocks cost 7+c_plus+c_minus dynamic
instructions, where c_plus=1[u+v>=p] and c_minus=1[u>=v]. Their static cost is 9.

Write h=popcount(floor(bw/p)), c=c_plus+c_minus. The fused body costs 40+h+c;
the duplicated body costs 73+2h+c. With setup, cleanup and accept:
  fused:     95+h+c <=113; static length 113;
  duplicated:128+2h+c<=162; static length 162;
  exact saving: 33+h instructions, between 33 and 49.
All upper bounds are attained by u=b=w=65536. The improvement pays the retained
v's initialization, use and erasure. It removes a complete reduction as well as
a multiplication. A repeated-butterfly program pays setup/cleanup only once;
the caller must also pay its literal constants, routing, array loads/stores,
normalization, output delivery and any other kernel work. This local saving is
not a whole-job complexity or kappa comparison.

4. FastPoly syntax application
The independent circuit_sharing.py mirrors the wire/mul/add/sub/fork/bind
fragment of FastPoly.Cost.Circuit; it does not import Lean or claim to be a
checked port. The duplicated syntax is fork(add(u,mul(b,w)),sub(u,mul(b,w))).
The shared syntax is bind(mul(b,w),fork(add(inl(u),inr(0)),sub(inl(u),inr(0)))).
Evaluating bind extends the original environment by the producer's output.
Both expressions therefore evaluate to (u+bw,u-bw) in every ring, directly by
the defining equations. The gates recurrence gives two multiplications and two
additions for the duplicated syntax, one multiplication and two additions for
the shared syntax. This is a fixed syntax for every input, respecting the
RealizesFamily quantifier order. RAM reduction/framing costs are then charged
separately as above; FastPoly gate counts are never called RAM instruction costs.

5. Evidence and exact remaining formalization boundary
verify_wordram.py checks all 65,537 b at a=65,536, crossing every quotient q from
0 to 65,535, plus 5,096 edge/random butterfly triples with dirty scratch and far
memory. It checks exact outputs, dynamic formulas, accepted halt, failure to halt
with one step less, write frames, scratch cleanup and signed indirect addressing.
circuit_sharing.py checks 2,197 signed integer triples and modular evaluations.
These are finite regression tests; the invariant arguments above provide the
separate informal universal claims.

A direct Lean proof should encode these exact emitted instruction lists as
List WordRAM.Instr, instantiate InRange 64 for each signed intermediate, compose
steps_straight/effect_mul/steps_bltz/Steps.trans for each block, and finish with
exec_of_steps, accept and the write-set frame theorem. This direct route avoids
inventing a Light compilation correspondence. compileProgram_correct has distinct
Light.Exec, Fits and Input hypotheses; it is not applied here, and its constant
compiler overhead cannot be identified with these hand-assembled exact counts.
The Python-to-Lean interpreter refinement and exact literal-program proofs remain
unformalized. No success of a Lean build or axiom audit is asserted.

This package's Python code and proofs are original independent descriptions.
Neither shared butterfly computation nor binary modular reduction is claimed
new. The useful contribution is a concrete, fully counted executable integration
with exact contracts, overflow ranges, dirty-memory frames and regression evidence.
